headline: Chip Rout Drags the Tape Lower as Homebuilders Stand Alone
body_html:
Stocks are leaning lower at midday on Monday, with 431 of the 666 names we track falling and only 228 rising. The damage is lopsided. Semiconductors are down 4.43%, easily the weakest group on the board and the main source of pressure on the broader market.

Beyond chips, the losses spread to other cyclical corners. Financials are off 2.25% and energy has given up 1.62%, while software and materials are each lower by 0.89%. Industrials are down 0.43%. Healthcare (down 0.12%) and consumer (down 0.26%) are holding up comparatively well, and homebuilders are the only group in positive territory, up 0.37%.

The standout mover is MiniMed Group, up 5.89% and leading the gainers. On the downside, MaxLinear is down 8.08%, Sandisk 7.99% and Credo Technology 7.23%. Into the close, the question is whether the chip selling exhausts itself or spreads further, and whether financials stabilize before Tuesday, November 17. These prices are not final and can still move.

briefs.headline: Chip Names Take the Brunt of the Selling
briefs.body: MaxLinear, Sandisk, PDF Solutions, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor, Credo Technology and Semtech all sit among the biggest decliners, each down more than 7%. The weakness reaches memory, power, analog and connectivity, so this is a sector-wide retreat rather than a single-name problem.

briefs.headline: Financials Slip More Than 2%
briefs.body: The financial group is down 2.25%, the second-worst sector on our board after semiconductors. With 431 stocks lower against 228 higher across our universe, the pullback is not confined to technology. Whether banks and lenders steady themselves is a key watch item into the close.

briefs.headline: MiniMed Leads the Winners
briefs.body: MiniMed Group is up 5.89%, the best gain among the names we track. The medical-device company is bucking a soft tape, and healthcare as a whole is only slightly lower, down 0.12%. Genmab and Indivior are also among the leaders, each up more than 2%.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Hold the Only Green Sector
briefs.body: Homebuilders are up 0.37%, the one group in positive territory while chips, financials and energy slide. The gain is modest, but it stands out on a day when most sectors are lower and may reflect investors rotating away from the hardest-hit areas.

briefs.headline: Defensive Consumer Names Find Buyers
briefs.body: Tractor Supply is up 2.88%, Starbucks up 2.37% and John B. Sanfilippo & Son up 2.61%. All three are among the top gainers. The pattern suggests some money moving toward steadier consumer-facing businesses while the technology complex sells off.

briefs.headline: Crypto Wobbles After a Forced-Selling Wave
briefs.body: Bitcoin dropped sharply after a cascade of forced liquidations, then bounced slightly. Risk appetite looks fragile across assets. Meanwhile, Gulf markets have recovered earlier losses despite regional security worries, a small sign of stability outside the U.S. equity tape.
